key_insight: A single monolithic lattice Boltzmann formulation can model both free-fluid and heterogeneous porous regions in one domain while correctly capturing porosity-scaled pressure, convection, and viscous stress.
engineering_relevance: This enables efficient simulation of coupled flow through and around porous structures for device-scale design, where porosity varies spatially and fluid–porous interfaces must be handled consistently.
method: Uses a standard-lattice LBM with one kinetic equation for weakly compressible, isothermal flow.
Adds Darcy-Forchheimer drag, Brinkman-like viscous stress, variable-porosity corrections, and generalized forcing in a unified framework.
Allows independent tuning of sound speed and effective bulk viscosity to improve efficiency and stability.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on 2D benchmark flow problems and shown to reproduce free-fluid/porous interactions within a one-domain solver.
watch_item: Accuracy and stability likely depend on careful parameterization of porosity, drag, and forcing terms, especially near sharp fluid–porous transitions.
paper_title: Monolithic kinetic algorithm for heterogeneous porous media systems using a continuous one-domain approach
